# Wi-Fi Heatmapper

> Free, open-source (MIT) desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux that measures Wi-Fi signal strength, and optionally TCP/UDP throughput with iperf3, at the spot you click on a floor plan, then draws heat maps of the results. Everything stays on the user's computer. Current version: {{VERSION}}.

Source code, issues and releases: https://github.com/hnykda/wifi-heatmapper (repository name `hnykda/wifi-heatmapper`). The documentation is Markdown in that repository (`docs/guide/`), published as HTML at https://wifi-heatmapper.danielalder.cz/docs/<page> with a Markdown copy at /docs/<page>.md, the links below. https://wifi-heatmapper.danielalder.cz/llms-full.txt contains the whole guide in one file.

Key facts:

- Install: download from https://github.com/hnykda/wifi-heatmapper/releases/latest (`.dmg` for macOS, `-setup.exe` or `.msi` for Windows, `.deb` or `.AppImage` for Linux, x64 and ARM64), or `brew install --cask hnykda/tap/wifi-heatmapper` on macOS. The apps are unsigned, so macOS and Windows warn on first launch.
- From source: Node.js 20+, `git clone https://github.com/hnykda/wifi-heatmapper.git && cd wifi-heatmapper && npm install && npm run dev`, then http://localhost:3000. `npm run dev:mock` uses synthetic measurements (no Wi-Fi, sudo or iperf3 needed).
- Signal is read with CoreWLAN through a bundled helper on macOS (Location access needed to see the network name), the Native Wifi API (`wlanapi.dll`) on Windows, and `iw` on Linux. Throughput needs `iperf3` on this computer and `iperf3 -s` on another computer on the network.
- Workflow: Settings (floor plan, iperf3 server) -> Floor plan (click where you stand to measure) -> Heat maps (adjust radius, fixed colour scales, download PNG) -> Survey points (table, CSV export).
- Data: one JSON file per floor plan. In the desktop app under the OS's app data folder (see Installing the app); from source in `data/` (override with `WIFI_HEATMAPPER_DATA_DIR`).
- Bug reports: https://github.com/hnykda/wifi-heatmapper/issues/new/choose with the details from the app's About dialog and a log (`LOG_LEVEL=2`).

## Development

- [CONTRIBUTING](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hnykda/wifi-heatmapper/main/CONTRIBUTING.md): setup, test suites (`npm run verify`, `npm run e2e`), code layout, what a pull request needs
- [CLAUDE.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hnykda/wifi-heatmapper/main/CLAUDE.md): short orientation for coding agents working in the repository
- [Architecture](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hnykda/wifi-heatmapper/main/docs/dev/architecture.md): code layout, platform `WifiActions`, routes, how the UI and server talk, Windows localization, heat map rendering
